Medicaid Programs; Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act; Interoperability Standards and 
Prior Authorization for Drugs for Medicare Advantage Organizations, Medicaid Managed Care 
Plans, State Medicaid Agencies, Children's Health Insurance Program (CHIP) Agencies and CHIP

analysis:
## 1. COMMENTER INFORMATION

- **Author/Organization name:** Massachusetts Health Data Consortium (MHDC) — Denny Brennan, Executive Director
- **Stakeholder type:** Technology Vendor / Other (nonprofit health IT and data organization; neutral convener; operates New England Healthcare Exchange Network / NEHEN)
- **Credentials or expertise mentioned:** More than four decades of advancing health information exchange, interoperability, and administrative simplification across Massachusetts and nationally; operates NEHEN providing secure data exchange for thousands of health professionals; direct operating experience onboarding payers and providers to FHIR IGs in production; planning a Drug PA Implementation demonstration pilot in partnership with Point-of-Care Partners.

---

## 2. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

MHDC broadly supports CMS's direction toward electronic PA for drugs using FHIR and NCPDP standards, recommending at minimum 18 months post-final rule before compliance (replacing the October 1, 2027 target) and establishment of a national FHIR-enabled endpoint registry as a prerequisite to testing at scale. MHDC favors retiring the legacy X12N 278 on an aligned timeline, preserving NCPDP standards for pharmacy benefit ePA and Da Vinci CRD/DTR/PAS for medical benefit ePA under a clear single routing rule, and requiring coded structured denial reasons. MHDC also raises incentive misalignment (payers face hard January 2027 API deadlines while EHR vendors and providers do not) and offers extensive recommendations on event notifications, payer API accountability, step therapy, lab/DMEPOS PA extension, and cybersecurity.

---

## 3. REGULATORY CONTEXT

- **Specific provisions addressed:** PA-DRUG-MEDICAL, PA-DRUG-PHARMACY, FHIR-IG-REQUIRED, HIPAA-PA-STANDARDS, API-ENDPOINT-REPORTING, API-USAGE-METRICS, PA-DENIAL-REASONS, ONC-STANDARDS-UPDATE, GENERAL (RFIs: event notifications, payer API, step therapy, lab/DMEPOS, cybersecurity)
- **Regulatory citations mentioned:** 42 CFR §422.122(a) (MA denial reason requirement); CMS-0057-F (2024 Interoperability and Prior Authorization rule); ONC January 1, 2028 standards expiration; January 1, 2027 payer API deadline; MIPS attestation incentive (2027); 42 CFR Part 2; October 1, 2027 compliance date
- **Standards referenced:** HL7 Da Vinci CRD, DTR, PAS, CDex, Notifications IGs; NCPDP F&B, RTPB, SCRIPT, Telecommunications Standard; X12N 278, X12 270/271; HL7 FHIR Subscriptions; US Core / USCDI; NDH Endpoint Profile; HL7 Inferno test suite; FHIR PlanDefinition/ActivityDefinition; CDS Hooks; CQL

---

## 4. DETAILED POSITIONS

**Topic 1: Implementation Timelines and Prerequisites**
- **Provision ID:** PA-DRUG-MEDICAL, PA-DRUG-PHARMACY, FHIR-IG-REQUIRED
- **Position:** Modify
- **Rationale:** October 1, 2027 is premature. January 1, 2027 enhancements from CMS-0057-F have not gone live yet; FHIR APIs have not been tested at scale; onboarding a single payer to a new FHIR IG takes up to 24 months end-to-end in NEHEN's direct experience. Health system compliance deadlines arrive before vendors are certified, creating compliance risks. Multiple IG versions require time for alignment, and health plans have been building earlier IG versions for two years.
- **Specific request:** Minimum 18 months post-final rule before compliance; allow plans to use prior standards versions until January 1, 2028; extend ONC's January 1, 2028 standards expiration requirement where vendors are mid-implementation; establish a national FHIR-enabled provider directory (NDH Endpoint Profile) as a prerequisite to testing at scale; require mandatory interoperability testing before production go-live.

**Topic 2: FHIR/NCPDP Dual Standard — Medical vs. Pharmacy Benefit Routing**
- **Provision ID:** PA-DRUG-MEDICAL, PA-DRUG-PHARMACY, MEDICAL-VS-PHARMACY-BENEFIT
- **Position:** Support / Clarify
- **Rationale:** NCPDP F&B, RTPB, and SCRIPT are appropriate for pharmacy benefit ePA; Da Vinci CRD/DTR/PAS for medical benefit ePA. CRD can complement RTBC to confirm benefit routing; FHIR can extract clinical criteria from EHR to enrich RTBC; CDS Hooks and CQL can drive question-sets within SCRIPT. The routing determination at the point of prescribing must be reliable and clear.
- **Specific request:** Preserve NCPDP F&B, RTPB, and SCRIPT for pharmacy benefit ePA; adopt Da Vinci CRD/DTR/PAS for medical benefit ePA; adopt a single routing rule so providers have a predictable path for determining which pathway applies; leverage NCPDP Telecommunications Standard and SCRIPT for real-time PA status updates across prescriber, payer, and PBM; encourage pharmacy/PBM-managed status updates to patients.

**Topic 3: X12N 278 Retirement / HIPAA FHIR Adoption**
- **Provision ID:** HIPAA-PA-STANDARDS
- **Position:** Support
- **Rationale:** MHDC supports retiring legacy X12N 278 and adopting FHIR-based standards for medical PA, attachments, referrals, and eligibility, but on an aligned timeline that avoids requiring payers to support two standards in parallel. Asking health plans to support two standards is not feasible. CDex should be used only when the Da Vinci DTR IG questionnaire cannot be used.
- **Specific request:** Retire X12N 278 and X12 270/271 and replace with FHIR; align timeline to avoid dual-standard burden; use CRD for eligibility/coverage-related PA; CDex only as fallback when DTR is not applicable.

**Topic 4: Denial Reasons**
- **Provision ID:** PA-DENIAL-REASONS
- **Position:** Support / Modify
- **Rationale:** Free-text denial reasons are insufficient for appeals, analytics, and quality improvement. Coded, structured denial reasons with optional free text extend the existing MA requirement (42 CFR §422.122(a)) into the pharmacy benefit and provide actionable information.
- **Specific request:** Require coded, structured denial reasons with optional free text drawn from a standard taxonomy covering: missing clinical documentation, step therapy not met (with specific alternatives and trial durations), diagnosis mismatch, quantity limit exceeded, non-covered drug, site-of-care restriction, benefit exclusion, medical necessity not established, duplicate therapy, payer needs additional information.

**Topic 5: API Endpoint Reporting and Registry**
- **Provision ID:** API-ENDPOINT-REPORTING
- **Position:** Support / Modify
- **Rationale:** Endpoint reporting is only useful if machine-readable and discoverable. Without an accurate national directory, endpoint discovery depends on manual, non-scalable processes (confirmed by NEHEN operations daily). A national FHIR-enabled registry aligned with NDH Endpoint Profile is the prerequisite that turns published API specifications into a usable network.
- **Specific request:** Require machine-readable national payer API endpoint reporting to a FHIR-enabled registry aligned with NDH Endpoint Profile; require metadata including payer name/plan IDs, API use case, endpoint URL, FHIR version, supported IG versions, auth method, registration process, sandbox availability, production status, and change history. Establish a glide path away from portal-only PA; portals should not satisfy interoperability goals indefinitely.

**Topic 6: Incentive Misalignment**
- **Provision ID:** PA-DRUG-MEDICAL, FHIR-IG-REQUIRED
- **Position:** Clarify / Modify
- **Rationale:** Under CMS-0057-F, payers face a hard January 1, 2027 deadline for APIs to be operational, but EHR developers face no equivalent deadline and providers face no mandate (only a MIPS attestation incentive starting 2027). This misalignment means payer investments cannot be utilized by providers and reduces effectiveness of the overall interoperability ecosystem.
- **Specific request:** Align incentives across health plans, providers, and system developers; ensure prescribers can choose formulary-approved drugs upfront to reduce back-and-forth; synchronize clinical screening between prescribers and pharmacists; align provider reimbursement incentives with workflow efficiency.

**Topic 7: Payer API Implementation Improvement (RFI)**
- **Provision ID:** API-USAGE-METRICS, API-ENDPOINT-REPORTING, GENERAL
- **Position:** Support / Modify
- **Rationale:** NEHEN observes daily the gap between published specifications and usable production networks: API endpoints documented but not reachable, capability statements diverging from actual behavior, authentication flows breaking in production, IG versions drifting between trading partners.
- **Specific request:** Require independent conformance testing against relevant IGs (not self-attestation) using Da Vinci reference implementations and HL7 Inferno; require machine-readable endpoint registry (NDH profile); require quarterly machine-readable API performance metrics (volume, response time, error rate, auth-failure rate by use case); explicitly recognize aggregated networks (HIEs, QHINs, regional exchanges like NEHEN) as conforming intermediaries.

**Topic 8: Event Notifications (RFI)**
- **Provision ID:** GENERAL
- **Position:** Support
- **Rationale:** ADT and high-value clinical event notifications are among the most operationally valuable forms of payer-provider exchange; value scales with participation breadth and data consistency. Today's notification landscape is fragmented; a federal floor would address gaps without displacing working regional infrastructure.
- **Specific request:** Adopt HL7 FHIR Subscriptions and Da Vinci Notifications IG as HIPAA standard transport for event notifications; define minimum event set (at minimum ADT and ED encounter); recognize HIEs, QHINs, and aggregated networks as conforming delivery channels; align notification payload with USCDI; provide explicit patient consent and notification suppression guidance (42 CFR Part 2, state behavioral health privacy, patient opt-outs).

**Topic 9: Step Therapy (RFI)**
- **Provision ID:** GENERAL
- **Position:** Support (with conditions)
- **Rationale:** Step therapy creates avoidable burden because prescribers cannot see step therapy requirements at the point of prescribing, what alternatives have been tried, or what the exception pathway looks like, resulting in trial-and-error prescribing and duplicate appeals.
- **Specific request:** Require step therapy requirements exposed through FHIR/NCPDP standards at point of prescribing (CRD and RTBC as carriers); require plans to honor prior-trial documentation from standards-based ePA; require electronic step therapy exception pathway with parallel timeframes to PA (7-day standard / 72-hour urgent); require coded, structured denial reasons for step therapy denials.

**Topic 10: Lab Tests and DMEPOS (RFI)**
- **Provision ID:** GENERAL
- **Position:** Support
- **Rationale:** Lab and DMEPOS PA share the same operational pain points as drug PA; the same standards apply without category-specific reinvention. However, coverage policies and LCDs are not currently machine-readable, and DMEPOS involves a supplier intermediary distinct from the prescribing provider.
- **Specific request:** Extend Da Vinci CRD, DTR, PAS to lab and DMEPOS PA on the same timeline as medical PA; require coverage policies and LCDs to be published in machine-readable form (FHIR PlanDefinition/ActivityDefinition); clarify supplier role in standards-based workflow; set explicit real-time performance expectations for low-complexity lab PA decisions.

**Topic 11: Cybersecurity / Resiliency (RFI)**
- **Provision ID:** GENERAL
- **Position:** Support / Modify
- **Rationale:** Removing or restructuring privacy/security certification without clearly defined replacement baselines may weaken trust. Aggregated, governed exchange infrastructure (like NEHEN) reduces attack surface compared to bilateral point-to-point connections. AI-enabled Decision Support Interventions (DSIs) require governance and transparency expectations.
- **Specific request:** Specify minimum security expectations for API-based exchange (authentication, authorization, audit logging, incident response); provide transition plan to avoid security gap; retain targeted audit-related capabilities until replacements are mature; set clear vendor security expectations; retain DSI guardrails; outline transparency and governance expectations for AI-enabled DSIs.

---

## 5. SOLICITATION RESPONSES

- **S1 (FHIR-IG-REQUIRED - require vs. recommend IGs):** Supports requiring FHIR IGs for medical benefit ePA (CRD/DTR/PAS) while preserving NCPDP for pharmacy benefit; notes dual-standard burden and advocates for clear routing rule.
- **S2/S3 (FHIR-IG-REQUIRED - IG versions/transitions):** Recommends allowing plans to use prior IG versions until January 1, 2028; notes health plans are mid-build on earlier versions; stresses importance of IG version alignment time.
- **S12 (PA-DRUG-MEDICAL - technical challenges):** Documents NEHEN's direct experience: onboarding a single payer to a new FHIR IG takes up to 24 months; FHIR APIs have not been tested at scale; January 2027 enhancements have not yet gone live.
- **S15 (PA-DRUG-MEDICAL - medical vs. pharmacy distinction):** Provides detailed routing analysis: NCPDP F&B/RTPB/SCRIPT for pharmacy benefit; Da Vinci CRD/DTR/PAS for medical benefit; recommends single routing rule; identifies intersection opportunities for CRD + RTBC and FHIR-based clinical criteria enrichment.
- **S16/S17 (PA-DENIAL-REASONS - what is specific reason / structured codes):** Strongly opposes free-text denial reasons; recommends coded, structured denial taxonomy with optional free text; provides a specific 10-category taxonomy.
- **S21 (PA-DRUG-MEDICAL - timeline achievable):** States October 1, 2027 is premature; recommends minimum 18 months post-final rule based on NEHEN's direct operating experience.
- **S23 (API-ENDPOINT-REPORTING - security concerns):** Recommends specifying minimum security expectations for API-based exchange; advocates for aggregated governed networks as a security baseline reducing point-to-point risk.
- **S24/S26/S27/S33 (API-ENDPOINT-REPORTING):** Recommends machine-readable endpoint registry aligned with NDH Endpoint Profile with comprehensive required metadata fields; glide path away from portal-only PA.
- **S29/S30/S34/S35 (API-USAGE-METRICS):** Recommends quarterly machine-readable API performance metrics (volume, response time, error rate, auth-failure rate by use case) with public reporting for accountability.
- **S44 (HIPAA-PA-STANDARDS - FHIR appropriate):** Supports retiring X12N 278 and adopting FHIR; notes CDex should be fallback when DTR is not applicable; requires sufficient time for industry to test at scale.
- **S46 (HIPAA-PA-STANDARDS - X12 coexistence):** Recommends aligned timeline that avoids requiring payers to support two standards in parallel; supporting two standards is not feasible.
- **S47 (HIPAA-PA-STANDARDS - timeline):** States 24-month HIPAA compliance period is insufficient given scale testing requirements; recommends minimum 18 months post-final rule.
- **S60/S61/S62/S63/S65 (ONC-STANDARDS-UPDATE):** Recommends extending ONC January 1, 2028 standards expiration; notes some vendors are mid-implementation; recommends mandatory interoperability testing before production go-live; supports IG version alignment time.
- **S66 (GENERAL RFI - event notifications):** Strongly supports FHIR Subscriptions and Da Vinci Notifications IG as federal floor for event notifications; recognizes intermediaries; aligns payload with USCDI; provides consent suppression guidance.
- **S67-S82 (GENERAL RFIs):** Step therapy: expose requirements via FHIR/NCPDP at point of prescribing, honor prior-trial documentation, require electronic exception pathway. Lab/DMEPOS: extend Da Vinci IGs, require machine-readable LCDs, clarify supplier role. Cybersecurity: minimum API security expectations, transition plan, AI/DSI governance.

---

## 6. RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Provide at minimum 18 months post-final rule before compliance is required (replacing October 1, 2027).
2. Allow plans to use prior IG standard versions until January 1, 2028; extend ONC's standards expiration requirement for vendors mid-implementation.
3. Establish a national, FHIR-enabled provider directory aligned with the NDH Endpoint Profile as a prerequisite to testing at scale.
4. Require mandatory interoperability testing before production go-live; provide educational resources and technical support for smaller organizations.
5. Preserve NCPDP F&B, RTPB, and SCRIPT for pharmacy benefit ePA; adopt Da Vinci CRD/DTR/PAS for medical benefit ePA; implement a single routing rule.
6. Retire legacy X12N 278 and adopt FHIR-based standards for PA, attachments, referrals, and eligibility on an aligned timeline that avoids requiring payers to support two standards in parallel.
7. Require coded, structured denial reasons with optional free text drawn from a standard 10-category taxonomy.
8. Use CDex only when DTR questionnaire cannot be used.
9. Require machine-readable payer API endpoint reporting to an NDH-aligned FHIR-enabled national registry with comprehensive metadata fields.
10. Establish a glide path away from portal-only PA; portals cannot substitute for standards-based exchange.
11. Align incentives across payers, EHR vendors, and providers (currently only payers face hard API deadlines).
12. Require independent FHIR API conformance testing (not self-attestation) using Da Vinci reference implementations and HL7 Inferno.
13. Require quarterly machine-readable API performance metrics with public reporting.
14. Explicitly recognize aggregated networks (HIEs, QHINs, regional exchanges) as conforming intermediaries for API obligations.
15. Adopt HL7 FHIR Subscriptions and Da Vinci Notifications IG as HIPAA standard for event notifications; define minimum event set; recognize HIEs/QHINs/aggregated networks as conforming delivery channels.
16. Require step therapy requirements exposed via FHIR/NCPDP at point of prescribing; honor prior-trial documentation; require electronic exception pathway with parallel PA timeframes.
17. Extend Da Vinci CRD/DTR/PAS to lab and DMEPOS PA; require machine-readable LCDs; clarify DMEPOS supplier role; set real-time performance expectations for lab PA.
18. Specify minimum API security expectations; provide transition plan to avoid security gap; retain DSI guardrails; establish AI/DSI governance and transparency expectations.

---

## 7. CONCERNS & OBJECTIONS

- **Primary concerns:** October 1, 2027 compliance date is premature given scale testing requirements and unfinished January 2027 CMS-0057-F milestones; incentive misalignment (payers face hard deadlines, providers/EHR vendors do not) undermines ecosystem effectiveness; removing certification criteria without replacement creates fragmentation risk and security gaps; portal exceptions allow indefinite avoidance of standards-based exchange.
- **Potential negative impacts cited:** Health system compliance deadlines arriving before vendors are certified creates operational and compliance risks; requiring payers to support two standards in parallel is not feasible; removing interoperability floor risks bespoke integrations and inconsistent vendor behavior; point-to-point connections increase security attack surface versus aggregated governed networks.
- **Implementation barriers mentioned:** No operational national endpoint directory (manual processes cannot scale to nationwide ePA mandate); FHIR APIs not yet tested at scale; onboarding a single payer to FHIR IG takes up to 24 months in NEHEN's experience; nearly half of PA requests still rely on phone/fax despite declining fax usage.

---

## 8. SUPPORTING EVIDENCE

- **Data or statistics cited:** 95% of surveyed physicians say PAs delay care; 94% link PAs to burnout; 26% report serious adverse events; NEHEN onboarding experience: single payer to new FHIR IG takes up to 24 months end-to-end; nearly half of PA requests still rely on phone/fax; NEHEN has 20+ payers and 260+ provider organizations participating.
- **Studies or research referenced:** Cited footnote [i]: "ePA Explained: NCPDP SCRIPT & Surescripts Prior Authorization | IntuitionLabs" (source of physician PA survey data).
- **Examples provided:** NEHEN as aggregated multi-payer, multi-provider exchange operating for 20+ years; Drug PA Implementation demonstration pilot planned in partnership with Point-of-Care Partners (4 testable hypotheses, 7–8 month duration, 6 phases, 3 formal decision gates).

---

## 9. IMPACT ASSESSMENT

- **Affected stakeholders:** MA organizations, Medicaid/CHIP managed care, QHP issuers, PBMs, EHR vendors, pharmacies, providers (including smaller practices and rural providers), HIEs, QHINs, DMEPOS suppliers, labs, patients.
- **Economic implications:** Incentive misalignment means payer API investments cannot be utilized, reducing return on compliance investment; aggregated networks reduce per-participant cost compared to bilateral integrations; requiring two standards in parallel (FHIR + X12) imposes duplicative development costs; portal-only exception allows continued avoidance of standards-based exchange investment.
- **Technical feasibility:** MHDC has direct experience showing onboarding single payer to FHIR IG takes up to 24 months; Burden Reduction FHIR APIs not yet tested at scale; national endpoint directory is prerequisite for scaling to nationwide mandate; FHIR Subscriptions and Da Vinci Notifications IG are ready for event notification standardization.
- **Patient care impact:** 95% of physicians say PAs delay care; 26% report serious adverse events from PA delays; real-time ePA and formulary visibility at point of prescribing would reduce avoidable prescribing errors, delays, and administrative burden; step therapy information visibility at point of prescribing prevents trial-and-error prescribing.

---

## 10. SENTIMENT ANALYSIS

- **Overall position:** Supportive (with significant modifications on timeline, prerequisites, and implementation approach)
- **Tone:** Professional, Technical, Collaborative
- **Priority level:** High

---

## 11. KEY QUOTES

1. "The central challenge is no longer technical feasibility, but operational ease and scalability of data exchange for PA." - Context: Framing MHDC's perspective on the current state of interoperability maturity and what CMS-0062-P needs to solve.

2. "A national, FHIR-enabled provider directory aligned with the National Directory of Healthcare Providers & Services (NDH) Endpoint Profile is the prerequisite that turns CMS's ePA APIs from a published specification into a usable network." - Context: Explaining why the endpoint registry must be established before testing at scale can occur.

3. "Onboarding a single payer to a new FHIR IG can take up to 24 months end-to-end...An October 1, 2027, compliance date will not allow that work to be done well; a minimum 18-month post-final-rule window will." - Context: Drawing on NEHEN's direct operating experience to justify the timeline recommendation.

4. "Without an aggregated model, the operational burden of bilateral arrangements falls hardest on the smaller payers and provider organizations that CMS's rule is meant to bring into the standards-based ecosystem." - Context: Arguing that CMS should affirmatively support aggregated exchange models rather than bilateral connections.

---

## 12. THEMES

- [x] **IMPLEMENTATION-TIMELINE** - Central theme: October 1, 2027 is premature; recommends minimum 18 months post-final rule based on NEHEN's direct experience; addresses ONC January 2028 standards expiration and need for IG version alignment time.
- [x] **COST-RESOURCES** - Aggregated models reduce per-participant costs vs. bilateral; requiring dual standards (FHIR + X12) imposes duplicative development costs; incentive misalignment reduces return on payer compliance investment.
- [x] **PROVIDER-BURDEN** - Addresses incentive misalignment leaving providers without mandate to adopt; step therapy visibility at point of prescribing reduces avoidable burden; lab/DMEPOS PA extension reduces phone/fax dependence.
- [x] **PRIVACY-SECURITY** - Detailed cybersecurity section: recommends minimum API security specifications; warns against removing certification criteria without replacement; advocates for aggregated governed networks as superior security model vs. point-to-point; AI/DSI governance and transparency.
- [ ] **HEALTH-EQUITY** - Implicitly addressed: small/rural providers benefit from aggregated model and portal exception during transition; not a primary focus.
- [x] **TECHNICAL-FEASIBILITY** - Extensive: NEHEN operating experience documents 24-month payer onboarding; FHIR APIs not tested at scale; endpoint directory prerequisite; IG version alignment needed; Drug PA pilot planned.
- [x] **STANDARDS-MATURITY** - Recommends IG version alignment time; plans should use prior versions until January 2028; conformance testing required before production go-live; CDex only as DTR fallback.
- [x] **PATIENT-ACCESS** - Cites 95% physician PA delay rate and 26% serious adverse events; real-time ePA improves formulary visibility and reduces prescribing errors; step therapy prior-trial documentation prevents unnecessary retreatment.
- [ ] **REGULATORY-AUTHORITY** - Not directly addressed.
- [x] **STAKEHOLDER-COORDINATION** - Incentive misalignment between payers, EHR vendors, and providers; recommends CMS-ONC coordination; explicit recognition of HIEs/QHINs as conforming intermediaries; MHDC Drug PA pilot to generate evidence for CMS.
- [x] **MEDICAL-VS-PHARMACY-BENEFIT** - Detailed routing analysis: NCPDP for pharmacy benefit, FHIR for medical benefit; recommends single routing rule at point of prescribing; identifies NCPDP-FHIR intersection opportunities.
- [x] **TRANSPARENCY** - Strongly supports structured denial reasons with standard taxonomy; endorses PA status visibility across prescriber, pharmacy, and payer via SCRIPT; quarterly API performance metrics with public reporting.
- [x] **SMALL-PAYER-IMPACT** - Notes operational burden of bilateral arrangements falls hardest on smaller payers and provider organizations; recommends aggregated model and portal exception for small/rural providers during transition.
- [x] **EXISTING-WORKFLOWS** - Supports retiring X12N 278 on aligned timeline; opposes dual-standard burden; recommends portal exception glide path; leverages existing NCPDP messaging standards for PA status.
- [x] **VENDOR-ECOSYSTEM** - Notes EHR vendors mid-implementation of earlier IG versions; health system compliance deadlines arrive before vendors are certified; requires independent conformance testing; recognizes NEHEN as production aggregated exchange model.
